name: Split Power Right
purpose: Off-tackle power to the far back, who crosses behind the quarterback and takes a deep handoff. Our end drives their end out, the playside guard takes the man over him or doubles the nose and climbs — whichever the front gives him — and the near back leads up through the hole.

QB.rule: Open playside and hand deep to the back crossing behind you. Let him come to you, then fake away.

LH.rule: Cross behind the quarterback, take the handoff deep, then press our tackle's outside hip. Turn up inside the blocks.

coaching_points: Identical blocking to Split Counter. The line learns one set of rules and gets two plays out of it — say that out loud when you install the second one.
The near back's block in the hole is the play. He takes the first man who shows in it rather than a man picked before the snap. Drill it on its own.
The carrier travels further than the blocker, and that is the point — he arrives behind the lead, not beside it.
If the handoff is late, the quarterback is reaching. He holds the ball still and lets the back run through it.

Against the 4-4 nobody is assigned to their outside linebacker — the near back is leading into the hole and has to take him if he fills. Against the 5-4-2 the Z screens that linebacker himself. If he keeps making the tackle either way, the answer is the Pitch: it gets outside him instead of running at him.
